category: Core verbs: cleaning and the home

entries.meaning: Mop has 2 distinct senses.
examples: I mop the kitchen twice a week.
Someone mopped the hallway and left it wet.
He was mopping the floor when the phone rang.
He mops his forehead between rounds.
She mopped her face with a paper towel.
The old man sat mopping his brow in the heat.

senses.head: To wash a floor with a mop
examples: I mop the kitchen twice a week.
Someone mopped the hallway and left it wet.
He was mopping the floor when the phone rang.

senses.head: To wipe sweat or water off your face or skin with a cloth
examples: He mops his forehead between rounds.
She mopped her face with a paper towel.
The old man sat mopping his brow in the heat.

entries.русский: мыть шваброй, вымыть шваброй; вытирать, вытереть (пот с лица)
entries.contrast: The p doubles: mopped, mopping — compare hoped, hoping, where the long vowel keeps one p.

entries.meaning: To clean a floor or a rug with a vacuum cleaner. ---
examples: Could you vacuum the living room?
I already vacuumed upstairs.
She's vacuuming, so she can't hear you.
entries.transitivity: both — transitive (vacuum the rug), intransitive (he vacuums on Fridays)
entries.contrast: Two u's in the middle: vacuum, not vacum or vaccum.

entries.meaning: Dust has 2 distinct senses.
examples: I need to dust the bookshelves.
She dusted the whole room before the guests arrived.
He's dusting the picture frames.
Dust the cake with powdered sugar before serving.
She dusted the pan with flour.
Snow had dusted the fields overnight.

senses.head: To wipe the dust off furniture and shelves
examples: I need to dust the bookshelves.
She dusted the whole room before the guests arrived.
He's dusting the picture frames.

senses.head: To sprinkle a fine powder lightly over something
examples: Dust the cake with powdered sugar before serving.
She dusted the pan with flour.
Snow had dusted the fields overnight.

entries.русский: вытирать пыль, вытереть пыль; посыпать; посыпать, припорошить
entries.transitivity: both — transitive (dust the shelves), intransitive (she dusts every week)
entries.contrast: Dust the shelf means take dust off, but dust the cake with sugar means put a fine layer on — the same verb, opposite directions.

entries.meaning: Scour has 2 distinct senses.
examples: You'll have to scour the pan to get the burned rice off.
He scoured the sink until it was white again.
She spent an hour scouring the grill.
Volunteers scour the beach after every storm.
We scoured three stores looking for that part.
They have scoured every record in the archive.

senses.head: To clean a surface by rubbing it hard with something rough
examples: You'll have to scour the pan to get the burned rice off.
He scoured the sink until it was white again.
She spent an hour scouring the grill.

senses.head: To search a place or a list very thoroughly
examples: Volunteers scour the beach after every storm.
We scoured three stores looking for that part.
They have scoured every record in the archive.

entries.русский: отдраивать, отдраить; оттирать, оттереть; прочёсывать, прочесать; тщательно обыскивать, обыскать

entries.meaning: To polish something with a soft cloth until it shines. ---
examples: Buff the wood with a dry cloth.
He buffed the faucet until it gleamed.
The floors had been buffed that morning.

entries.meaning: Launder has 2 distinct senses.
examples: The hotel launders the towels every day.
She laundered the curtains before hanging them back up.
Freshly laundered sheets smell wonderful.
They laundered the cash through a chain of car washes.
It is not easy to launder that much money.
He admitted laundering more than a million dollars.

senses.head: To wash and iron clothes or linens
examples: The hotel launders the towels every day.
She laundered the curtains before hanging them back up.
Freshly laundered sheets smell wonderful.

senses.head: To pass money from crime through legal businesses so that it looks honest
examples: They laundered the cash through a chain of car washes.
It is not easy to launder that much money.
He admitted laundering more than a million dollars.

entries.contrast: In the news launder also means to hide dirty money — launder money — so context decides the sense.

entries.meaning: To make something white or lighter with a strong chemical. ---
examples: Don't bleach that shirt — it's colored.
He bleached the kitchen towels.
The sun had bleached the curtains almost white.
entries.contrast: After -ch the third person takes -es: bleaches.

entries.meaning: Sanitize has 2 distinct senses.
examples: The restaurant sanitizes the tables between customers.
She sanitized the baby bottles.
They were sanitizing the carts at the door.
Textbooks often sanitize the ugliest parts of the war.
The agency sanitized the report before releasing it.
We only got a sanitized version of what happened that night.

senses.head: To clean something so that it is free of germs
examples: The restaurant sanitizes the tables between customers.
She sanitized the baby bottles.
They were sanitizing the carts at the door.

senses.head: To remove the parts of a story or a document that might offend or reveal too much
examples: Textbooks often sanitize the ugliest parts of the war.
The agency sanitized the report before releasing it.
We only got a sanitized version of what happened that night.

entries.русский: дезинфицировать, обеззараживать, обеззаразить; приглаживать, подчищать (текст, версию событий); вымарывать
entries.contrast: American spelling sanitize; the British write sanitise.

entries.meaning: To remove a bad smell from a place or a thing. ---
examples: Baking soda will deodorize the fridge.
She deodorized the carpet after the dog got sick.
They're deodorizing the whole basement.

entries.meaning: To make a room or a thing smell and feel clean again. ---
examples: A little vinegar will freshen the drain.
She freshened the guest room with clean sheets and an open window.
Candles were freshening the air after dinner.

entries.meaning: To rub soap into a foam, or to make foam. ---
examples: This shampoo doesn't lather much.
He lathered his hands and scrubbed.
The soap was lathering nicely under the hot water.
entries.transitivity: both — transitive (lather your hands), intransitive (this soap lathers well)

entries.meaning: To wash hair or a carpet with shampoo. ---
examples: I shampoo my hair every other day.
They shampooed the living room carpet.
She's shampooing the dog in the tub.
entries.contrast: The final -oo simply adds -ed: shampooed, never shampoed.

entries.meaning: Comb has 2 distinct senses.
examples: Comb your hair before we leave.
She combed the tangles out slowly.
He was combing the rug for a lost earring.
Volunteers comb the beach after every storm.
Detectives combed the apartment for fingerprints.
We have combed the records twice and found nothing.

senses.head: To pull a comb through hair to make it neat
examples: Comb your hair before we leave.
She combed the tangles out slowly.
He was combing the rug for a lost earring.

senses.head: To search a place very carefully and completely
examples: Volunteers comb the beach after every storm.
Detectives combed the apartment for fingerprints.
We have combed the records twice and found nothing.

entries.русский: расчёсывать, расчесать; прочёсывать; прочёсывать, прочесать; тщательно обыскивать
entries.contrast: The b is silent: KOHM, like home with a k.

entries.meaning: To make cloth smooth with a hot iron. ---
examples: I hate to iron shirts.
She ironed the tablecloth before the dinner.
He was ironing when I called.
entries.transitivity: both — transitive (iron a shirt), intransitive (he irons while watching TV)
entries.contrast: Said EYE-urn, not EYE-ron — the r is heard before the vowel, not after it.

entries.meaning: To stiffen cloth with starch while washing or ironing it. ---
examples: The cleaners starch his collars.
She starched the napkins for the wedding.
He wore a heavily starched white shirt.

entries.meaning: To fold and sew the edge of cloth so it does not fray. ---
examples: Could you hem these pants?
She hemmed the curtains an inch shorter.
The dress still needs hemming.
entries.contrast: The m doubles: hemmed, hemming.

entries.meaning: To let fresh air move through a room. ---
examples: Open a window to ventilate the room while you paint.
They ventilated the basement for two days.
The bathroom isn't well ventilated.

entries.meaning: To put things back where they belong so a place looks neat. ---
examples: Tidy your desk before you leave.
She tidied the kitchen in ten minutes.
He was tidying the garage all afternoon.
entries.русский: убирать, убрать; наводить порядок, навести порядок
entries.transitivity: both — transitive (tidy your desk), intransitive (he tidies before guests come)
entries.contrast: Consonant + -y: tidies, tidied, but tidying keeps the y.

entries.meaning: To make something straight or neat. ---
examples: Straighten the pictures on the wall.
He straightened the chairs after the meeting.
She's straightening the shelves in the hall closet.
entries.contrast: The gh is silent: STRAY-tuhn.
entries.phrasal verbs: straighten out · straighten out · straighten up

entries.meaning: To put things in a different order or place. ---
examples: Let's rearrange the living room.
He rearranged the kitchen cabinets over the weekend.
She keeps rearranging the furniture.

entries.meaning: To get rid of things you do not need so a space feels open again. ---
examples: We should declutter before we move.
She decluttered the whole basement in January.
They're decluttering one drawer at a time.
entries.transitivity: both — transitive (declutter the desk), intransitive (we decluttered all weekend)

entries.meaning: Smooth has 2 distinct senses.
examples: Smooth the sheet before you tuck it in.
She smoothed the wrinkles out of the tablecloth.
He was smoothing the bedspread with both hands.
A good agent smooths the way for first-time buyers.
Her recommendation smoothed his path into the program.
They are trying to smooth the transition for laid-off workers.

senses.head: To flatten something by running your hand over it
examples: Smooth the sheet before you tuck it in.
She smoothed the wrinkles out of the tablecloth.
He was smoothing the bedspread with both hands.

senses.head: To make a process easier by removing the problems from it
examples: A good agent smooths the way for first-time buyers.
Her recommendation smoothed his path into the program.
They are trying to smooth the transition for laid-off workers.

entries.русский: разглаживать, разгладить; сглаживать, сгладить; сглаживать, облегчать (процесс); устранять препятствия
entries.contrast: The th is voiced, as in this, not as in think.

entries.meaning: To push the loose end of cloth into a narrow space so it stays. ---
examples: Tuck the sheet under the mattress.
She tucked the price tags out of sight.
He was tucking the blanket around the edges of the crib.
entries.phrasal verbs: tuck away · tuck in · tuck in

entries.meaning: To hang cloth loosely over something. ---
examples: Drape a towel over the chair to dry.
She draped a sheet over the couch before painting.
A blanket was draped across the back of the sofa.

entries.meaning: Place has 3 distinct senses.
examples: Place the glasses upside down on the towel.
He placed the vase in the center of the table.
The boxes were placed along the far wall.
You can place an order online or by phone.
He placed a small bet on the last race.
The ad was placed in three local papers.
I know that face, but I can't place it.
It took her a minute to place his accent.
He finally placed the man as a neighbor from years ago.

senses.head: To put something carefully in a particular spot
examples: Place the glasses upside down on the towel.
He placed the vase in the center of the table.
The boxes were placed along the far wall.

senses.head: To formally make an order, a bet, or an advertisement
examples: You can place an order online or by phone.
He placed a small bet on the last race.
The ad was placed in three local papers.

senses.head: To remember where you know someone or something from
examples: I know that face, but I can't place it.
It took her a minute to place his accent.
He finally placed the man as a neighbor from years ago.

entries.русский: класть, положить; помещать, поместить; размещать, разместить (заказ, объявление); делать, сделать (ставку); вспомнить (откуда знаешь), узнать

entries.meaning: Sort has 2 distinct senses.
examples: Sort the whites from the colors.
He sorted the mail into three piles.
She's sorting the recycling.
Sort the list by date and print it.
She sorted the emails by sender.
The files are sorted alphabetically.

senses.head: To separate things into groups of the same kind
examples: Sort the whites from the colors.
He sorted the mail into three piles.
She's sorting the recycling.

senses.head: To arrange things in a particular order, such as by date or alphabetically
examples: Sort the list by date and print it.
She sorted the emails by sender.
The files are sorted alphabetically.

entries.русский: сортировать, рассортировать; разбирать, разобрать; упорядочивать, сортировать (по дате, по алфавиту)
entries.transitivity: both — transitive (sort the mail), intransitive (we sorted for an hour)
entries.phrasal verbs: sort out · sort out · sort through

entries.meaning: To put a lot of things on top of each other, usually not neatly. ---
examples: Don't pile the dishes in the sink.
He piled the dirty laundry by the door.
Papers were piled on every chair.
entries.русский: сваливать в кучу, свалить; наваливать, навалить
entries.phrasal verbs: pile into · pile on · pile up

entries.meaning: Shelve has 2 distinct senses.
examples: The library pays students to shelve books.
She shelved the canned goods by date.
He was shelving the new arrivals all morning.
The city shelved plans for a new stadium.
If the funding falls through, they will shelve the whole project.
The bill has been shelved until after the election.

senses.head: To put things away on a shelf
body: (ставить на полку, поставить; раскладывать по полкам)
examples: The library pays students to shelve books.
She shelved the canned goods by date.
He was shelving the new arrivals all morning.

senses.head: To decide not to continue with a plan or project, at least for now
examples: The city shelved plans for a new stadium.
If the funding falls through, they will shelve the whole project.
The bill has been shelved until after the election.

entries.русский: ставить на полку, поставить; раскладывать по полкам; откладывать, отложить (проект, план); класть под сукно
entries.contrast: The noun shelf turns its f into v: one shelf, two shelves, and the verb is shelve.

entries.meaning: To put things into groups by type. ---
examples: Categorize the tools by size.
He categorized the receipts by month.
The files have been categorized and boxed.

entries.meaning: To put things together because they belong to the same set. ---
examples: Group the cleaning supplies on one shelf.
She grouped the photos by year.
The chairs were grouped around the fireplace.

entries.meaning: Box has 2 distinct senses.
examples: We need to box the books before Friday.
He boxed the china in newspaper.
Everything in the attic has been boxed and labeled.
He boxed in college and still trains twice a week.
They box three rounds on Friday night.
She has been boxing since she was twelve.

senses.head: To pack things into boxes
body: (упаковывать в коробки, упаковать; укладывать в коробку)
examples: We need to box the books before Friday.
He boxed the china in newspaper.
Everything in the attic has been boxed and labeled.

senses.head: To fight with the fists as a sport
examples: He boxed in college and still trains twice a week.
They box three rounds on Friday night.
She has been boxing since she was twelve.

entries.русский: упаковывать в коробки, упаковать; укладывать в коробку; боксировать, заниматься боксом
entries.contrast: After -x the third person takes -es: boxes.

entries.meaning: Bag has 2 distinct senses.
examples: Bag the leaves and leave them at the curb.
She bagged the old clothes for donation.
He's bagging groceries at the store.
They hope to bag two turkeys this fall.
He bagged a twelve-point buck on the last day of the season.
She's bagged the biggest account in the office.

senses.head: To put something into a bag
body: (складывать в пакет, сложить; упаковывать в мешок)
examples: Bag the leaves and leave them at the curb.
She bagged the old clothes for donation.
He's bagging groceries at the store.

senses.head: To catch or kill an animal while hunting, or informally, to succeed in getting something
examples: They hope to bag two turkeys this fall.
He bagged a twelve-point buck on the last day of the season.
She's bagged the biggest account in the office.

entries.русский: складывать в пакет, сложить; упаковывать в мешок; добывать (на охоте), подстрелить; заполучить, урвать (разг.)
entries.contrast: The g doubles: bagged, bagging.

entries.meaning: To put something away in a safe or hidden place. ---
examples: Stash the extra batteries in that drawer.
He stashed the wrapping paper behind the couch.
She had stashed a spare key under the mat.

entries.meaning: To throw something away because it is no longer wanted. ---
examples: Discard anything that's expired.
She discarded three bags of old paperwork.
The packaging can be discarded.
entries.contrast: The verb is dis-KAHRD; the noun, a thing thrown away, is DIS-kahrd.

entries.meaning: Recycle has 2 distinct senses.
examples: We recycle glass and cardboard.
He recycled the newspapers.
This bag is made from recycled plastic.
Don't just recycle last year's talk.
He recycled the same joke at every stop on the tour.
That plot has been recycled a dozen times.

senses.head: To send used paper, glass, or plastic to be made into something new
examples: We recycle glass and cardboard.
He recycled the newspapers.
This bag is made from recycled plastic.

senses.head: To use old material or old ideas again instead of making something new
examples: Don't just recycle last year's talk.
He recycled the same joke at every stop on the tour.
That plot has been recycled a dozen times.

entries.русский: перерабатывать, переработать; сдавать на переработку; использовать повторно (идеи, материал); повторять, перелицовывать
entries.transitivity: both — transitive (recycle the bottles), intransitive (we recycle)

entries.meaning: To let food scraps and leaves rot so they turn into soil. ---
examples: We compost all our vegetable peels.
She composted the coffee grounds.
They've been composting since spring.
entries.transitivity: both — transitive (compost the peels), intransitive (they compost)

entries.meaning: Dump has 2 distinct senses.
examples: Don't dump the toys on the floor.
He dumped the dirty water in the yard.
She was dumping the ashtray into the trash.
She dumped him over the phone.
If he keeps lying, she will dump him.
He was dumped two weeks before the wedding.

senses.head: To empty something out quickly and carelessly
examples: Don't dump the toys on the floor.
He dumped the dirty water in the yard.
She was dumping the ashtray into the trash.

senses.head: To suddenly end a romantic relationship with someone (informal)
examples: She dumped him over the phone.
If he keeps lying, she will dump him.
He was dumped two weeks before the wedding.

entries.русский: вываливать, вывалить; сваливать, свалить; выбрасывать; бросать, бросить (партнёра)

entries.meaning: Empty has 2 distinct senses.
examples: Empty the trash before you go.
He emptied the vacuum bag outside.
She's emptying the dishwasher.
The Mississippi empties into the Gulf of Mexico.
Two small streams emptied into the lake behind the house.
The canal emptying into the harbor was dug in 1830.

senses.head: To take everything out of a container
examples: Empty the trash before you go.
He emptied the vacuum bag outside.
She's emptying the dishwasher.

senses.head: To flow into a larger body of water, said of a river or a stream
examples: The Mississippi empties into the Gulf of Mexico.
Two small streams emptied into the lake behind the house.
The canal emptying into the harbor was dug in 1830.

entries.русский: опорожнять, опорожнить; опустошать; выносить (мусор); впадать (о реке, ручье)
entries.transitivity: both — transitive (empty the trash), intransitive (the room emptied fast)
entries.contrast: Consonant + -y: empties, emptied, but emptying keeps the y.

entries.meaning: To use something again instead of throwing it away. ---
examples: We reuse the jars for storage.
She reused the gift bags.
This container can be reused many times.
entries.contrast: The verb ends in /z/ — ree-YOOZ; the noun reuse ends in /s/ — ree-YOOSS.

entries.meaning: To drop trash where it does not belong, or to cover a place with scattered things. ---
examples: Please don't litter.
Toys littered the hallway.
The floor was littered with wrapping paper.
entries.transitivity: both — transitive (toys littered the hall), intransitive (please don't litter)

entries.meaning: To make liquid fly about in drops, or to fly about in drops. ---
examples: Try not to splash when you fill the bucket.
Soapy water splashed onto the floor.
The kids were splashing in the tub.
entries.transitivity: both — transitive (splash water on it), intransitive (water splashed on the floor)

entries.meaning: To force liquid out in a thin fast stream. ---
examples: Squirt a little soap into the sink.
He squirted cleaner on the stovetop.
The bottle was squirting sideways.
entries.transitivity: both — transitive (squirt some soap), intransitive (the bottle squirted sideways)

entries.meaning: To make a dirty or blurred mark by rubbing something. ---
examples: Don't smudge the mirror.
She smudged the fresh paint with her sleeve.
The chrome was smudged with fingerprints.
entries.transitivity: both — transitive (smudge the mirror), intransitive (wet ink smudges)

entries.meaning: To make something dirty. ---
examples: Grass will soil white pants in a minute.
One picnic soiled the new tablecloth.
The soiled towels go straight into the hamper.
entries.contrast: Soiled is the word on laundry labels and in hospitals; as a noun, soil means почва.

entries.meaning: Dampen has 2 distinct senses.
examples: Dampen the cloth before you dust.
She dampened the shirt and ironed it flat.
He was dampening the sponge under the faucet.
The rain didn't dampen their enthusiasm.
Higher rates dampened demand for houses.
Bad reviews are dampening ticket sales.

senses.head: To make something slightly wet
examples: Dampen the cloth before you dust.
She dampened the shirt and ironed it flat.
He was dampening the sponge under the faucet.

senses.head: To make a feeling or an effect weaker
examples: The rain didn't dampen their enthusiasm.
Higher rates dampened demand for houses.
Bad reviews are dampening ticket sales.

entries.русский: увлажнять, увлажнить; смачивать, смочить; ослаблять, умерять (пыл), подпортить

entries.meaning: To make something a little wet. ---
examples: Moisten the stain, then blot it.
She moistened the label to peel it off.
The steam had moistened the whole wall.
entries.contrast: The t is silent: MOY-suhn, like listen and fasten.

entries.meaning: Absorb has 3 distinct senses.
examples: These towels absorb a lot of water.
The rag absorbed most of the spill.
The paper was absorbing the oil.
It takes time to absorb so much new material.
She absorbed everything the coach told her.
I was still absorbing the news when the phone rang.
Good running shoes absorb the shock of each step.
The company absorbed the extra cost instead of raising prices.
The foam panels are absorbing most of the noise from the street.

senses.head: To take in liquid so that it is no longer on the surface
examples: These towels absorb a lot of water.
The rag absorbed most of the spill.
The paper was absorbing the oil.

senses.head: To take in information and understand it
examples: It takes time to absorb so much new material.
She absorbed everything the coach told her.
I was still absorbing the news when the phone rang.

senses.head: To take in force, shock, or a cost so that it does less damage
examples: Good running shoes absorb the shock of each step.
The company absorbed the extra cost instead of raising prices.
The foam panels are absorbing most of the noise from the street.

entries.русский: впитывать, впитать; поглощать, поглотить; усваивать, усвоить; воспринимать (информацию); поглощать, смягчать (удар); принимать на себя (расходы)
entries.contrast: The s is pronounced /z/: ub-ZORB, not ub-SORB.

entries.meaning: To press a cloth or paper onto a wet spot so the liquid soaks in. ---
examples: Blot the spill — don't rub it.
She blotted the wine with a napkin.
He was blotting the carpet with a clean towel.
entries.contrast: The t doubles: blotted, blotting.

entries.meaning: To touch something lightly and repeatedly with a cloth or a finger. ---
examples: Dab a little soap on the stain.
She dabbed at the spot with a wet cloth.
He was dabbing the paint off his hands.
entries.transitivity: both — transitive (dab the stain), intransitive (she dabbed at the spot)
entries.contrast: The b doubles: dabbed, dabbing.

entries.meaning: Immerse has 2 distinct senses.
examples: Immerse the jars in boiling water for ten minutes.
She immersed the sponge and squeezed it out.
The base of the kettle must never be immersed in water.
Immerse yourself in the material before the exam.
She immersed herself in the language for a year.
He has immersed himself in local politics since he retired.

senses.head: To put something completely under a liquid
examples: Immerse the jars in boiling water for ten minutes.
She immersed the sponge and squeezed it out.
The base of the kettle must never be immersed in water.

senses.head: To become completely involved in an activity or a subject
body: (погружаться, погрузиться (с головой во что-л.); уходить с головой)
examples: Immerse yourself in the material before the exam.
She immersed herself in the language for a year.
He has immersed himself in local politics since he retired.

entries.русский: погружать, погрузить; окунать, окунуть; погружаться, погрузиться (с головой во что-л.); уходить с головой

entries.meaning: To put oil on something so that it moves smoothly or does not dry out. ---
examples: Oil the hinge and the squeak will stop.
He oiled the cutting board once a month.
She's oiling the wooden spoons.

entries.meaning: To clear a blocked pipe or drain. ---
examples: Vinegar and baking soda can unclog a slow drain.
He unclogged the shower with a piece of wire.
She spent an hour unclogging the kitchen sink.

entries.meaning: Plunge has 2 distinct senses.
examples: You may have to plunge the toilet.
He plunged the drain until the water went down.
She was plunging the sink when I walked in.
Temperatures plunge after sunset in the desert.
The bus skidded and plunged into the river.
Stock prices have plunged since the announcement.

senses.head: To clear a blocked toilet or drain with a plunger, or to push something down into liquid
examples: You may have to plunge the toilet.
He plunged the drain until the water went down.
She was plunging the sink when I walked in.

senses.head: To fall or drop suddenly and steeply
examples: Temperatures plunge after sunset in the desert.
The bus skidded and plunged into the river.
Stock prices have plunged since the announcement.

entries.русский: прочищать вантузом; погружать, погрузить; резко падать, обрушиться; рухнуть
entries.transitivity: both — transitive (plunge the toilet), intransitive (he plunged for ten minutes)

entries.meaning: Flush has 2 distinct senses.
examples: Flush the toilet twice if you have to.
He flushed the radiator hose with clean water.
The toilet won't stop flushing.

senses.head: To send water through something to clean it out, especially a toilet
examples: Flush the toilet twice if you have to.
He flushed the radiator hose with clean water.
The toilet won't stop flushing.

senses.head: To turn red in the face from heat, embarrassment, or strong feeling
examples: She flushed when he read her name out loud.
His face flushes whenever he has to speak in public.
Her cheeks were flushed from the cold.

entries.русский: смывать, смыть (в туалете); промывать, промыть; краснеть, покраснеть; заливаться румянцем, вспыхнуть
entries.transitivity: both — transitive (flush the toilet), intransitive (the toilet won't flush)

entries.meaning: Strip has 2 distinct senses.
examples: Strip the beds and start a load of sheets.
He stripped the old wax off the floor.
They're stripping the wallpaper in the hall.
The board can strip him of his license.
The court stripped her of custody.
He was stripped of the gold medal.

senses.head: To take everything off a surface or a bed
examples: Strip the beds and start a load of sheets.
He stripped the old wax off the floor.
They're stripping the wallpaper in the hall.

senses.head: To take an official title, right, or position away from someone
examples: The board can strip him of his license.
The court stripped her of custody.
He was stripped of the gold medal.

entries.русский: снимать, снять (бельё, покрытие); сдирать, содрать; лишать, лишить (звания, прав, полномочий)
entries.contrast: The p doubles: stripped, stripping — striped, with one p, means в полоску.
entries.phrasal verbs: strip down · strip down · strip off

entries.meaning: Bathe has 2 distinct senses.
examples: It's easier to bathe the dog outside.
She bathed the twins one at a time.
He was bathing the baby when the doorbell rang.
Streetlights bathe the parking lot in a cold blue glow.
The sunset bathed the whole valley in orange.
The room was bathed in candlelight.

senses.head: To wash someone, or yourself, in a tub
examples: It's easier to bathe the dog outside.
She bathed the twins one at a time.
He was bathing the baby when the doorbell rang.

senses.head: To cover something completely in light or color
examples: Streetlights bathe the parking lot in a cold blue glow.
The sunset bathed the whole valley in orange.
The room was bathed in candlelight.

entries.русский: купать, искупать; мыться, купаться; заливать (светом), залить; окутывать
entries.transitivity: both — transitive (bathe the baby), intransitive (she bathes at night)
entries.contrast: The verb bathe is BAYTH, with a long a and a voiced th; the noun bath is BATH, short.

entries.meaning: Filter has 2 distinct senses.
examples: This pitcher filters the tap water.
She filtered the used frying oil through a cloth.
The air is filtered before it goes back into the room.
Sunlight filtered through the blinds.
News of the layoffs filtered through the office by noon.
Voices from the hallway kept filtering into the room.

senses.head: To pass liquid or air through something that takes the dirt out
examples: This pitcher filters the tap water.
She filtered the used frying oil through a cloth.
The air is filtered before it goes back into the room.

senses.head: To move slowly and in small amounts through or into a place
examples: Sunlight filtered through the blinds.
News of the layoffs filtered through the office by noon.
Voices from the hallway kept filtering into the room.

entries.русский: фильтровать, отфильтровать; очищать, очистить; просачиваться, просочиться; проникать (постепенно), пробиваться
entries.transitivity: both — transitive (filter the water), intransitive (light filtered through the blinds)

entries.meaning: To take the paper or covering off something.
examples: Unwrap the dishes carefully.
She unwrapped the glasses and washed each one.
He was unwrapping a package of new sponges.
entries.contrast: The w is silent and the p doubles: unwrapped, unwrapping.
